title: My AI trading model built from scratch on DGX Spark.
author: Dirty6996
selftext:
Hey everyone, new to the sub. I recently set up a DGX Spark and decided to put its local compute to use by launching a 30-day autonomous paper trading experiment. Instead of hardcoding a traditional quantitative strategy, I built a custom Python stack connected to the Alpaca API and gave the LLM "brain" a $1,000 balance, a baseline instruction prompt, and complete freedom to adapt on its own. Early on, it ran into major risk-management bottlenecks—repeatedly dumping massive chunks of cash into just one or two tickers and refusing to cut losses when they dipped, leaving it cash-poor and unable to capitalize on new market opportunities.

The logs show it's slowly adapting its capital allocation, but as a rudimentary system, I'm highly open to suggestions on how to improve its multi-step financial reasoning. I'd love tips on the best ways to prompt an agent to natively grasp position sizing and dynamic stop-losses without hardcoding strict indicator rules, as well as recommendations on which local models handle these trading loops best. *(Fun side note: Being a sci-fi nerd, I completely themed the agent's logic around the Ferengi Rules of Acquisition—though right now it definitely needs to learn Rule #192: Unbusinesslike directions lie on the road to ruin).*
